text:
Mika Zibanejad joined some elite Rangers company on Nov. 11, scoring twice in Calgary in what The New York Times noted was the Rangers' final visit to the Saddledome. Those were two of his five goals in 22 games. He has 19 points, mostly assists, and the scoring has lagged the reputation of a player with more than 800 career points.

The concern is chance quality, not luck. His expected goals (the quality of his looks) are down to 0.69 per 60 minutes from 1.02 last season, and he is finishing right about where those chances say he should. The Rangers also get just 44.7% of the shot attempts at five-on-five with him on the ice. Our numbers still see a 2.28 to 3.01 points-per-60 player, and he sits at 2.54, inside that range.

His one-timer is still there: a top shot speed in the 97th percentile, per NHL Edge. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming from the power play, so watch the man advantage. That is where his goals have always come from, and where to look first.
headline: Zibanejad's goals have been slow to arrive
